blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing international logistics in practice is managing detail under pressure. Every shipment lives inside a paperwork pack, a set of local rules, a deadline and a chain of people who may or may not answer the phone at the right moment. When one link misses a step, the whole container waits — and the cost clock runs regardless.

Good international teams build three habits. They prepare the paperwork before the goods move, not during. They use a single shared checklist across regions, so the same fields are filled in the same way. And they escalate early: by the time a problem is visible at the port, the fix needed was probably a phone call three days earlier.

None of this is glamorous. All of it is the quiet work of keeping containers moving when the world around them does not want them to.

items.q: According to the text, what happens when one person in the chain misses a step?
options: The whole container waits while the cost clock keeps running
The paperwork is rewritten
The shipment is rerouted to another port
The deadline is automatically extended
items.why: "the whole container waits — and the cost clock runs regardless." Um elo falho para o contêiner inteiro.

items.q: Why do good teams use a single shared checklist across regions?
options: To avoid using the phone
So the same fields are filled in the same way everywhere
To reduce the number of documents
To make the paperwork look more professional
items.why: "a single shared checklist across regions, so the same fields are filled in the same way."

items.q: What does "escalate early" mean in this context?
options: Raise a problem before it becomes visible at the port
Add more people to the chain
Increase the value of the shipment
Move goods faster than scheduled
items.why: "the fix needed was probably a phone call three days earlier" — agir antes do sintoma aparecer no porto.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Logistics work is exciting and glamorous
Preparing paperwork before goods move saves time later
A single field filled inconsistently can hold up a container
The most useful action is often taken days before the problem is seen
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz claramente "None of this is glamorous" — é trabalho silencioso, não glamoroso.

items.q: The phrase "the quiet work of keeping containers moving" suggests that…
options: only technology can keep shipments on schedule
containers move on their own if left alone
the real value comes from unglamorous, careful detail work
logistics is mostly about impressive, visible achievements
items.why: Inferência: o valor está no trabalho invisível e cuidadoso, não em feitos visíveis.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James fazer o debrief de um contêiner que ficou parado no porto. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, the debrief on container 4471. It sat at the port for four days, and I want everyone to understand exactly why, because it was not a customs problem and it was not the shipping line.

One field on the export document — the commodity code — was filled in differently in our Rotterdam office and our Singapore office. The port system flagged the mismatch, and the container was held until we could confirm which code was correct.

Here is the part that matters. When I called Rotterdam, they said they had followed their local template. When I called Singapore, they told me they had used the regional one. Both were sure they were right, and both were using a different checklist. Nobody was lying — we simply never agreed on one version.

The fix, in the end, was a two-minute email. But we found that out on day four, not on day zero. If either office had flagged the difference when the booking was made, the container would have sailed on time. From now on, one checklist, every region, no exceptions.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did container 4471 sit at the port for four days?
options: One field was filled in differently in two offices
The commodity code did not exist
The shipping line cancelled the booking
A customs officer refused to release it
items.why: "the commodity code — was filled in differently in our Rotterdam office and our Singapore office."

items.q: When James called each office, what did they report?
options: Both admitted they had made a mistake
Each said they had followed a different checklist and was sure they were right
Neither office answered the phone
Both blamed the port system
items.why: Rotterdam seguiu o template local; Singapura usou o regional — checklists diferentes, ambos convictos.

items.q: How long did the actual fix take, once found?
options: A full week
Three days
About two minutes
Four days
items.why: "The fix, in the end, was a two-minute email." — o custo foi o tempo, não o conserto.

items.q: What does James imply by saying "Nobody was lying"?
options: Someone in the chain was actually hiding the truth
The problem was a process gap, not dishonesty
The port system made a false report
The offices should be disciplined for the error
items.why: Inferência: a falha foi de processo (nenhum checklist único acordado), não de má-fé das pessoas.

items.q: What is the main lesson James wants the team to take away?
options: Avoid shipping through Rotterdam in future
Let the port system decide the codes
Flag differences early and use one shared checklist across regions
Stop using export documents altogether
items.why: Inferência: "one checklist, every region, no exceptions" e sinalizar a diferença no momento do booking.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Send me the full paperwork pack before the goods leave the warehouse." A paperwork pack is…
options: a box used to ship samples
the complete set of documents for a shipment
a customs officer
a team of clerks
items.why: Paperwork pack = pacote de documentos que acompanha o embarque.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Each country has its own rules, so a shipment must satisfy every ___ it passes through."
options: checklist
deadline
port
jurisdiction
items.why: Jurisdiction = jurisdição: o conjunto de regras legais de cada território.

items.q: "While the container was held, the cost clock kept running." The cost clock refers to…
options: the time zone at the destination
the shipping schedule
the charges that accumulate for every hour of delay
the delivery deadline
items.why: Cost clock = contador de custo: as despesas que sobem enquanto a carga espera.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When the desk clerk cannot resolve it, we ___ the issue to the regional manager."
options: postpone
translate
escalate
confirm
items.why: To escalate = escalar: levar o problema a um nível superior de decisão.

items.q: "Most of this job is quiet work nobody notices." Quiet work here means…
options: work that can be skipped safely
part-time administrative tasks
unglamorous, careful effort that prevents problems
work done in silence to avoid noise
items.why: Quiet work = trabalho silencioso: o esforço discreto que evita atrasos caros.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem na coordenação de logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The compliance team still has to sign off on the export documents." To sign off on means to…
options: reject them
print them
formally approve them
translate them
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the single checklist to every region next month." To roll out means to…
options: test it in secret
cancel it gradually
implement it across the operation
explain it to customs
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva em toda a operação.

items.q: "Singapore pushed back on switching to the new code." They…
options: rewrote the whole document
forgot about it
accepted it immediately
resisted or objected to the change
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de uma proposta.

items.q: "They agreed to align the templates but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to completion
asked another team to do it
did it ahead of schedule
did it twice by mistake
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "If the offices had flagged up the mismatch at booking, the container would have sailed on time." To flag up means to…
options: hide it from the manager
raise it so others notice and act
delay it deliberately
confirm it was correct
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar atenção para algo que precisa de ação.
